title: Pressure Sustaining Valve
model_title: Pressure Sustaining Valve (Pilot-Operated Diaphragm, Globe Pattern)

introduction.definition: A pressure sustaining valve maintains a minimum pressure UPSTREAM of itself. Its adjustable pilot senses inlet pressure: above the set point the pilot releases pressure from the control chamber and the main valve opens; below it, the pilot admits inlet pressure to the chamber and the valve throttles or closes. It keeps high areas of a network supplied, prevents pumps running out on their curves and holds back-pressure on processes.
applications: Water distribution zones and transfer mains
key_points: Modulating, hydraulically operated by line pressure
Needs clean water for the pilot circuit

classification.type: Hydraulically operated diaphragm globe valve with sustaining pilot

introduction.summary: A pressure sustaining (back-pressure) valve keeps the pressure UPSTREAM of it from falling below a set value. A small adjustable pilot senses inlet pressure: when inlet pressure rises above the set point the pilot vents the control chamber and the main valve opens further; when it falls, the pilot lets inlet pressure into the chamber and the main valve throttles. It protects high zones of water networks, prevents pump run-out and maintains back-pressure on processes.

steps.text: Inlet pressure acts under the disc and through the pilot circuit.
The pilot compares inlet pressure with its spring setting.
If inlet pressure rises above the set point the pilot vents the cover chamber and the disc opens.
If inlet pressure falls, the pilot fills the cover chamber; the spring and pressure push the disc towards the seat.
The disc settles in a position that holds the inlet pressure at the set point.

foundation: Support the valve and adjoining pipe so the body does not carry pipe weight or thermal loads; heavy valves need their own supports.
alignment: Align flanges face-to-face and bore-to-bore before bolting; never pull pipes into place with the bolts.
Respect the flow-direction arrow on the body.
piping: Install isolating valves and a strainer upstream of the pilot circuit.
Provide pressure gauges on inlet and outlet for setting.
commissioning: Check the valve strokes fully and smoothly.
Pressure-test the line (shell test) with the valve partly open; do not use the valve to blind a test above its seat rating.
Record the as-installed position and set points.

routine.task: Check inlet pressure holds at set point.

causes: Oversized valve, dirty needle valve, air in cover
remedies: Adjust speed control, bleed air, resize

video_tutorials.title: Pressure Sustaining Valve — Introduction

script.narration: This module introduces the Pressure Sustaining Valve.
A pressure sustaining valve maintains a minimum pressure UPSTREAM of itself.

Its adjustable pilot senses inlet pressure: above the set point the pilot releases pressure from the control chamber and the main valve opens; below it, the pilot admits inlet pressure to the chamber and the valve throttles or closes.
It keeps high areas of a network supplied, prevents pumps running out on their curves and holds back-pressure on processes.
Typical applications include water distribution zones and transfer mains; pump discharge (prevent run-out / cavitation); filter back-pressure; priority supply to elevated areas.
The cutaway reveals the internal construction: Globe Body with Seat Deck.
The exploded view separates every component so each one can be tapped for its function, material and failure modes.
Next, watch the operation tutorial to see how it works.

video_tutorials.title: Pressure Sustaining Valve — Operation

script.narration: How the Pressure Sustaining Valve works.
Inlet pressure acts under the disc and through the pilot circuit.
The pilot compares inlet pressure with its spring setting.
If inlet pressure rises above the set point the pilot vents the cover chamber and the disc opens.
If inlet pressure falls, the pilot fills the cover chamber; the spring and pressure push the disc towards the seat.
The disc settles in a position that holds the inlet pressure at the set point.
The flow overlay traces the liquid from suction to discharge.

video_tutorials.title: Pressure Sustaining Valve — Maintenance

script.narration: Maintenance essentials for the Pressure Sustaining Valve.
Check inlet pressure holds at set point.
Clean pilot strainer and restriction.
Inspect diaphragm, disc and seat.
Watch for hunting / instability: pressure oscillates. Common cause: oversized valve, dirty needle valve, air in cover.
Watch for fails to close: upstream pressure collapses. Common cause: torn diaphragm, debris on seat.
Watch for cavitation: noise, seat damage. Common cause: high ΔP at low flow.
Record every inspection so trends — vibration, temperature, leakage and performance — can be compared over time.
